# Skill catalog

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs` from templates/core/.claude/skills. Do not edit by hand. -->

The core skills agent-os installs in every project. On GitLab, `/pr` is installed as `/mr`, with `/pr` kept as an alias. The registry and vendored skills are in [skills.md](skills.md).

| Skill | What it does, and when it is used |
|---|---|
| `/pr` | Open a pull or merge request for the current branch only when it is ready (the gate passed on this exact commit, a journal entry, a non-empty Lessons section, a title in convention), then watch its checks and answer review threads. Use when a change is done, or when someone asks to open, update or follow a pull or merge request. |
| `/artifact` | Make an artifact (a self-contained page in artifacts/ - analysis, comparison, discovery, release report, retro, architecture, dashboard, stack map), build and verify it, and link it to the issues and pull or merge requests it belongs to. Use when a result reads better as a page than as Markdown, or when someone asks to share, check or link one. |
| `/audit` | Audit an idea, a spec, this project, a release, a problem or a system through separate lenses (product, architecture, stack, code quality, security and privacy, performance and cost, delivery, process, operations), each in its own subagent, and merge the findings into one report where every finding has evidence. Use when someone asks for an audit, a review of an idea or a codebase, or "what is wrong with X". |
| `/ci` | Write or review CI the way best practice asks (least-privilege permissions, pinned actions and images, timeouts, concurrency, no untrusted input in scripts, pull_request_target and OIDC rules), for platform. Use when someone adds or changes a workflow or pipeline, asks whether CI is safe, or a check behaves strangely. |
| `/discover` | Infer the conventions an active repository already follows (commit style, branch prefixes, merge strategy, areas) and the decisions made in its pull or merge requests, each with its evidence, then apply only what the person accepts. Use when agent-os is adopted in a repository with history, or when someone asks what this repository's conventions are. |
| `/doctor` | Check the agent system, the repository and the platform hygiene, repair what is mechanical, and propose the rest. Use when someone asks whether the setup is healthy, after an update, before a release, or when a hook or skill behaves strangely. |
| `/env` | Check that this laptop and this repository have what the project needs (MCP servers, command-line tools and their versions, platform token scopes, environment variables) and help fix what is missing. Use when a tool or MCP server is missing, a skill fails for an environment reason, someone joins the project, or before a release. |
| `/handoff` | End a session or a day so someone else (or you tomorrow) can continue - a status comment on each issue you hold with work in flight and one handoff journal entry. Use when someone says they are stopping, handing over, or going away. |
| `/ingest-docs` | Turn existing specifications into epics and sub-issues, each citing the section it came from, after reporting where the specifications contradict each other and asking the person how to resolve it. Use for a spec-first repository, or when someone asks to create the issues from the docs. |
| `/kickoff` | Start a new product - interview the person about the product, write the product doc, find the complexity level and the stack from the catalog's blueprints, then create the first milestone and issues from the doc. Use for a greenfield project, or when someone asks what to build a new product with. |
| `/lessons` | Capture, recall, search and triage lessons learned. Use when something went wrong or took long and should not happen again, when someone asks "what do we know about…", before working in an unfamiliar area, or to triage the lessons inbox without waiting for /retro. |
| `/next` | Recommend what to work on next from the repository's live state (your pull or merge requests that need you, reviews requested from you, your issues, free issues in the current milestone), each with a one-line reason, then offer /start. Use when someone asks what to do next, where to start, or what is most important now. |
| `/orchestrate` | Optional - coordinate several of your own sessions on this laptop - one session holds the orchestrator role, briefs worker sessions that each work one issue in their own worktree, and tracks them in a personal local ledger with typed messages (BRIEF, ACK, QUESTION, UPDATE, DONE, REVISE, CLOSE). Use only when the person runs several sessions and asks for one to coordinate; it never coordinates other people, who coordinate on platform. |
| `/release` | Release what is on {{branches.integration}} to {{branches.production}} - a release pull or merge request merged with a merge commit, a tag, the platform release with grouped notes, the rolling milestone rolled, release checks, and the sync back. Use only when the person asks to release or to ship a hotfix to production. |
| `/retro` | Triage the lessons inbox and repeated review findings into rule changes, active cards or rejections, and update the recall counters. Use at every release, when the Retro issue asks for it, or when someone asks to review the lessons. |
| `/runbook` | Keep a finished product safe to maintain and easy to take over - write the deploy, rollback and restore runbooks and the takeover dossier from the release flow, and run the upkeep audit (vulnerable dependencies, secrets, licenses) whose prioritized issues are filed only on confirmation. Use for a project in maintenance, before a handover, or when someone asks how to deploy, roll back or restore. |
| `/ship` | Merge a green, reviewed pull or merge request into {{branches.integration}}, close the issues it closes with a comment, keep the ones it only references open, set Done, and remove its branch and worktree. Use when someone says ship, merge or land a pull or merge request. |
| `/stack` | Explain, compare and change the project's stack map (stack.yaml) with the catalog's scores behind every recommendation - show it, compare two technologies, change a layer as a decision, detect or import it, keep it in step with the code. Use when someone asks what the project is built with, whether to switch a technology, or which option fits a layer. |
| `/standards` | Apply the project's coding standards - review a file or a diff against them, explain a rule, or choose between several ways to implement something and implement only the chosen one. Use before code review in /pr, when there is more than one reasonable implementation, or when someone asks whether code follows the standards. |
| `/start` | Start work on an issue the way the team can see it. Assign yourself, create its branch from the right base and link it to the issue, move it to In Progress and check it out. Use when someone says "start", "take", "pick up" or "work on" an issue, or after /next proposes one and the person agrees. |
| `/system` | Draft and keep up the system map (system.yaml) - components, where they live, what they expose and consume - from the repository's workspaces and manifests, asking where the code cannot tell. Use when someone asks how the project is put together, adds or splits a package or service, or before a security or architecture review. |
| `/test` | Plan test scenarios into an issue, run the suites a change needs, write the results into the pull or merge request, and find changed logic with no test. Use when an issue is created or started, before opening a pull or merge request, or when someone asks what to test. |
| `/ticket` | Create a complete issue (title convention, body from the form, one type and one priority label, one or more area labels, milestone, assignees, parent, blockers and test scenarios) after a duplicate search, in the issues language. Use when someone asks for a ticket or issue, or agrees to one you proposed. |
| `/upstream` | Propose an improvement to agent-os itself, as an issue on its public repository, with everything private removed and the exact text approved first. Use when someone says agent-os should do something better, when a lesson is about agent-os rather than the project, or when a doctor finding or a skill failure comes from the package. |
